title.title: The Partition Principle does not imply Choice
title.subtitle: Claim: if ZF is consistent, so is ZF with the Partition Principle and the failure of Choice

beats.text: PP: every surjection $X \to Y$ has an injection back $Y \to X$. Choice implies it
Schematic: does PP imply Choice? Open since Beppo Levi in 1902
The claim: a model of ZF where PP holds and Choice fails

sources.quote: If ZF is consistent then so is ZF + PP + AC_WO + not-AC, where PP says every surjection X -> Y admits an injection Y -> X.
PP traced to Beppo Levi (1902); whether PP implies AC is often called the oldest open problem in set theory

plain: Being able to reverse every onto-map does not give you the power to pick from every family of sets

steps: Start from an ordinary model of set theory with Choice
Add new sets by symmetric forcing, built from diagrams
Every partition maps back in, yet one family has no choice

voice.text: Choice implies the Partition Principle. Does the converse hold? Open since nineteen oh two.
Symmetric forcing builds a model where partitions inject back, yet choice fails.
Claimed: Partition does not imply Choice.
